source_controls.source: Science in Ancient Egypt, Papyrus Brooklyn 47.218.138, current scholarly edition
source_controls.finding: The papyrus contains a Ritual of Throwing the Balls. A rubric instructs recitation over four clay balls and throwing them toward south, north, west and east; variant procedures include water or binding to a papyrus roll and wearing it. The surrounding formula repels Seth from the divine body and characterizes the operation as great protection.

source_controls.source: Jean-Claude Goyon, Textes mythologiques II. Les revelations du mystere des Quatre Boules, BIFAO 75 (1975), pp.349-399

shared_features: inscribed containers / directional-protector corpus at Oxyrhynchus
relation_to_ue15307.interpretive_value: The four-ball ritual is a strong comparative control showing that ritual balls could operate as active directional apotropaic devices rather than merely passive symbolic cores.

epistemic_firewall: A parallel ritual using four clay balls does not identify the six UE15307 balls as thrown projectiles.
Do not force six archaeological boxes into a four-direction scheme.
Shared material/function is comparative evidence only, not provenance identity.
Exact UE15307 interpretation remains dependent on individual ficha and inscription recovery.
canonical_seal: THE ANCIENT RITUAL PROVES THAT A CLAY BALL COULD BE AN ACTIVE CARDINAL APOTROPAIC INSTRUMENT. IT DOES NOT YET PROVE WHAT EACH OF THE SIX CLOSED-NICHE OXYRHYNCHUS BALLS DID.
